basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '(Vers. 21.) Nephthalim virgultum resolutum, dans in generatione pulchritudinem. In'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 21.) Nephthalim virgultum resolutum, dans in generatione pulchritudinem. In Hebraeo ita scriptum est: Nephthalim ager irriguus, dans eloquia pulchritudinis, significans, quod aquae calidae in ipsa nascantur tribu: sive quod super lacum Genesareth, fluento Jordanis irrigua sit. Hebraei autem volunt, propter Tiberiadem, quae Legis videbatur habere notitiam, agrum irriguum, et eloquia pulchritudinis prophetari. Porro ubi nos agrum irriguum, et Septuaginta στέλεχος ἀνειμένον, id est virgultum resolutum posuerunt, in Hebraeo legitur AJALA SLUAA (אילה שלחה), quod potest et cervus emissus transferri, propter temporaneas fruges, velocitatem terrae uberioris ostendens. Sed melius, si ad doctrinam Salvatoris cuncta referamus quod ibi vel maxime docuerit, ut in Evangelio quoque scriptum est.
